title: POC ops timeline, bench checkpoints & exec readout - Orion Labs
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for Orion Labs' realtime summarization workload. Discussed success criteria (latency P95 <= 220ms, token cost target, fidelity on edge cases), access needs (VPC peering, test dataset, sample traffic), benchmark plan, mid-point review agenda, and exec readout expectations. Security questions flagged around KMS multi-tenant keys and SOC2 evidence. Action items and next steps agreed.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-15
Start: 09:32 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Lucas Bennett (Redwood Solutions); Maya Patel (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Ross (CTO, Orion); Marco Li (ML Engineer); Sana Ahmed (Security); Tom Reilly (Product); Asha Nair (SRE)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on POC milestones, success criteria, infra access and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the account. Big goal for today is to lock down the timeline and success criteria so we can start next week.
[00:18] Evelyn Ross: Hi Jordan, thanks. We're excited. We've got Marco, Sana, Tom and Asha on. Primary ask is to validate that Redwood can hit our realtime summarization latency and cost targets under our mixed user workload.
[00:35] Priya Desai: Quick intro from me — I'll be the SE running benchmarks and helping with infra. I'll propose the initial pod sizes and batch configs. A couple of notes: we do continuous batching and prefix cache at Redwood; sometimes transcribed as prefetch cache — ignore that.
[00:58] Marco Li: For context, our production traffic is spiky — 70th percentile small micro-summaries (~120 tokens) and 95th are long transcripts (~1,200 tokens) during peak. We need to size for both.
[01:22] Tom Reilly: And we need fidelity on edge cases like legal transcripts with bad audio; it's not just latency.
[01:45] Jordan Kim: Totally — so propose success criteria draft: 1) P95 latency <= 220ms for short requests (under 200 tokens) in our US region; 2) end-to-end cost per 1k short requests under $X (we'll propose number after we see sample traffic); 3) quality benchmark: >= 90% accept rate on 200 golden examples and no regressions on top-5 failure modes. Does that align?
[02:10] Evelyn Ross: P95 220ms is aggressive but acceptable if it doesn't blow cost. We'll trade off.
[02:35] Sana Ahmed: From security, we'll need to see SOC2 evidence, encryption details (KMS usage), and we want to understand key management: can Redwood support customer-managed keys for logs and model cache?
[03:00] Priya Desai: We do support KMS for request-at-rest encryption; for the private deployments we can integrate HSM. For hosted, we have a customer key option but the names sometimes get mangled in docs — I'll send the exact spec.
[03:21] Lucas Bennett: Also note that our KV cache naming is sometimes transcribed as 'K-V cash' in older docs, so watch for that in the security packet.
[03:40] Asha Nair: Network-wise we prefer VPC peering but we're OK with secure tunnel for the pilot. We'll share CIDRs.
[04:00] Jordan Kim: Proposed POC cadence: Week 0 (this week): kickoff + infra access; Week 1-2: benchmark baseline and smoke tests; Week 3-4: optimization—quantization/ batching / pod tuning; Week 5: mid-point review with engineering metrics and decision gate; Week 6: exec readout with business metrics and recommendation.
[04:30] Marco Li: That seems reasonable. For benchmarks, can you run both hosted and a Dedicated-equivalent to show cost/latency envelope?
[04:45] Priya Desai: Yes, plan is to run two tracks: hosted API baseline with our production-like request patterns and a Dedicated config which simulates reserved capacity (we'll approximate the Dedicated via a pinned pool in the same region). We'll report token cost, p95/p99 latency, throughput and failure rate.
[05:10] Tom Reilly: On quality metrics — we'll need a scoring rubric. We use a 0-2 'accept/rewrite' scale for summaries. Can you ingest our rubric?
[05:30] Priya Desai: Absolutely. Provide the rubric and golden sets; we'll hook it into the automated evals. We can also do a small A/B to surface differences between models/quantization.
[05:52] Jordan Kim: Good. Access checklist: 1) VPC details or jumpbox; 2) S3 test bucket with redacted telemetry; 3) service account for API keys; 4) allowlist of Redwood IPs (if peering not available). Asha, Sana — can you own infra access?
[06:15] Asha Nair: I can own it; I'll share CIDR and firewall rule doc. Expect that by 2026-08-18.
[06:30] Sana Ahmed: For compliance pack, what's the minimal artifact set? SOC2 report, data flow diagram, encryption spec and RBAC model?
[06:45] Maya Patel: We'll send our security pack — includes SOC2 Type II summary, encryption docs (KMS integration), SSO/SAML details and audit log samples. Note: some of the filenames in the pack had typos before; we'll check them.
[07:05] Jordan Kim: Great. Benchmarks — Priya, can you describe the synthetic traffic and load profile you'll run?
[07:20] Priya Desai: We'll run two scenarios: 1) steady-state 200 qps of small payloads to evaluate per-token cost, avg latency and P95; 2) spiky scenario with 10x bursts to validate autoscaling behavior and tail latency. We'll also run long-sequence runs to test KV cache hit behavior. The scripts will be shareable.
[07:48] Marco Li: For long sequences we care about memory and KV cache eviction — can you surface per-request KV hit ratio during tests?
[08:05] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll report KV cache hit ratio, average GPU utilization, and per-shard latency.
[08:20] Jordan Kim: Decision gates at mid-point: 1) Meets latency and cost targets on short requests; 2) No critical security blockers; 3) Exec sponsor comfortable with recommendation. If gate fails, we either extend or recommend Dedicated vs Hosted.
[08:42] Evelyn Ross: Who will we present to at the exec readout? CTO and VP Product will be there; if cost delta is material, CFO should join.
[08:58] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll prepare a 20-min readout + 15-min Q&A focused on metrics, cost model, and recommended next steps.
[09:12] Tom Reilly: On instrumentation — what dashboards will we get?
[09:25] Priya Desai: We'll provide a Grafana link with token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, KV hit ratio, and error traces. We'll email creds or set up cross-org read access.
[09:40] Sana Ahmed: A couple of security details: 1) how long do you retain logs for a POC? 2) Can you scrub logs automatically?
[09:53] Priya Desai: By default 30 days on hosted logs; we can reduce retention and add automatic PII redaction scripts. We'll document the scrub process.
[10:10] Jordan Kim: Pricing ask from Orion: they want a sense of cost per 1k short requests and per-1k long requests. We'll run bench and then provide a model with sensitivity to batch sizes and quantization.
[10:28] Marco Li: Also call out that sometimes we do stateful chains where the context grows — that'll affect cost; we need a model for incremental context costs.
[10:45] Priya Desai: We'll include a section on KV-based context vs naive re-send in the cost model.
[11:00] Jordan Kim: For the mid-point review agenda: quick re-cap, metrics and dashboards, incidents/observations, performance tuning done, recommendation for exec readout. Anyone want to tweak?
[11:16] Marco Li: Add an item for model quality failure modes and sample diffs.
[11:25] Priya Desai: Added. We'll surface sample outputs and their scores.
[11:35] Evelyn Ross: On dedicated vs hosted — advanced question: if we like Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[11:48] Jordan Kim: We can discuss committed capacity ranges; Maya will follow up with draft SOW/pricing options. For the POC we'll simulate a Dedicated-equivalent to show delta.
[12:05] Maya Patel: I'll put together an addendum with committed tiers and expected latency/cost ranges.
[12:18] Asha Nair: Minor ops note: we'll need a retro checklist post midpoint — who owns retesting after changes?
[12:30] Priya Desai: Redwood will run regression suite after any infra or model change; we'll coordinate with Marco for release windows.
[12:45] Tom Reilly: Anything else on timelines?
[12:50] Jordan Kim: Quick recap of dates: 1) Jordan sends runbook & network diagram by 2026-08-18; 2) Orion provides sample traffic and golden prompts by 2026-08-20; 3) Priya provides benchmark config by 2026-08-19; 4) Mid-point review week of 2026-09-07; 5) Exec readout week of 2026-09-14.
[13:12] Evelyn Ross: Works for us.
[13:20] Jordan Kim: Any blockers on security?
[13:26] Sana Ahmed: We'll need to review the encryption spec; depending on keys we may request customer-managed keys.
[13:36] Priya Desai: We'll include both hosted KMS option and Private deployment notes. For Private there's a different onboarding path and we can provision a customer key.
[13:52] Marco Li: Can you also capture model-version pinning and rollback playbook? We've had regressions with previous vendors when models auto-rolled.
[14:10] Lucas Bennett: We'll include a rollout/rollback playbook: pinned model versions, canary percentages, and automatic fallback to a baseline. We'll put that in the runbook.
[14:28] Tom Reilly: Great. Who's doing notes and artifacts?
[14:33] Jordan Kim: Maya will collect notes and share recording; Jordan will send runbook; Priya will share benchmark scripts.
[14:45] Jordan Kim: Final quick Qs — any competitor solutions you're testing?
[14:52] Evelyn Ross: We're running a limited eval with Anthropic and a small private infra test with AcmeInferenceCo. We want Redwood to show where it wins on unit cost and reliability.
[15:05] Jordan Kim: Understood — we'll make sure to surface direct comparisons where possible.
[15:18] Tom Reilly: Ok, let's do a quick risk register: 1) Access delays; 2) Security artifacts push; 3) Sample data not representative. How do we mitigate?
[15:35] Priya Desai: Mitigate with staged access — if VPC peering delayed, we'll use a tunnel and mock traffic. We'll also run a small local sample set to start tuning.
[15:50] Jordan Kim: Cool. Any late questions?
[16:00] Sana Ahmed: One last: audit logs — can you provide a sample log format so our compliance team can review?
[16:08] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll include sample audit logs in the security pack.
[16:20] Jordan Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate runbook and times for mid-point.
[16:28] Evelyn Ross: Thanks all.

Auto-generated action items (end): Jordan to send runbook; Priya to send bench scripts; Orion to provide samples; Maya to share SOW draft and security pack.

Meeting end: 10:29 PDT

Notes about transcript quality: some technical terms and product names were slightly mistranscribed (e.g., KV cache, KMS, Dedicated) — see security pack for canonical names.
